title: Venus in the Blind Spot
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A one-volume collection of ten Junji Ito horror short stories, including adaptations of Edogawa Ranpo's "The Human Chair" and "An Unearthly Love", the title story about a woman who becomes invisible to the men of her UFO club, and "The Enigma of Amigara Fault", in which people feel compelled to enter human-shaped holes in a cliff. It also includes a light autobiographical chapter about Ito and horror artist Kazuo Umezu.
life_message: No single ideal; the stories show obsession, possessiveness and the urge to belong turning destructive.

content.note: Gore and body horror (AniList tags); UFO club turns violent (ANN review).
Dread-driven horror anthology throughout (ANN review; AniList and MangaUpdates Horror).

Obsession, compulsion and tragic endings (ANN review; AniList Tragedy tag).
Stalking and hiding inside a chair to watch a woman shown as horror (ANN review).

Order vs freedom.evidence: No order or freedom argued; individuals undone by compulsion.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Title story shows a club of men fighting to possess one woman (ANN).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern settings; supernatural horror without religion.

folkways.japan: Draws on Japanese kaidan ghost tales and Edogawa Ranpo's ero-guro mystery tradition, described here as literary context.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewer infers themes of misogyny and isolation; stories end in dread without stated morals.
delivery.note: An anthology of horror tales whose themes readers must infer.

winners_losers: Most protagonists are undone by obsession or the uncanny; the title story's heroine meets a sorrowful end; sympathy rests with victims of possessiveness.
